title: Shared Memory-Aware Latency-Sensitive Message Aggregation for Fine-Grained Communication
problem: Message aggregation in HPC must balance reducing per-message communication overhead with minimizing message latency for fine-grained irregular messaging patterns in graph algorithms and parallel discrete event simulation.
motivation: Reducing message latency in PDES with speculative execution decreases costly rollbacks and improves overall application performance.
method: The technique bundles multiple messages together, which cuts the overhead of sending each one separately. It also considers where data lives in shared memory and places messages close to their destination (a strategy called locality awareness) to speed up delivery. By combining message batching with memory-aware placement, the approach reduces both the per-message overhead and end-to-end message latency. Validation used proxy applications that simulate realistic HPC workloads.
key_novelty: Message aggregation jointly optimizes for message latency and per-message overhead by accounting for shared memory characteristics.
contributions: Process-aware message aggregation schemes for fine-grained irregular communication
Joint optimization framework for messaging overhead and latency
Evaluation demonstrating effectiveness on graph algorithms and PDES proxy applications
Analysis of shared memory awareness in message aggregation design
limitations: Not discussed in the abstract provided.
primary_theme: process-aware message aggregation for latency-sensitive HPC
